post.title: Medallion Architecture: Bronze, Silver, and Gold Layers in Practice
post.subtitle: Structure your data lake with progressive refinement: raw Bronze ingestion, cleaned and conformed Silver, and business-ready Gold aggregates.
post.brief: Medallion Architecture solves the "data swamp" problem by organizing a data lake into three progressively refined zones — Bronze (raw, immutable), Silver (cleaned, conformed), Gold (aggregated, business-ready) — so teams always build on a trusted foundation, bad data never propagates silently, and any corruption can be replayed from scratch.

content.markdown:
## Scenario context

Medallion Architecture solves the "data swamp" problem by organizing a data lake into three progressively refined zones — Bronze (raw, immutable), Silver (cleaned, conformed), Gold (aggregated, business-ready) — so teams always build on a trusted foundation, bad data never propagates silently, and any corruption can be replayed from scratch.

> **TLDR** Three zones, one source of truth at every quality level: Bronze…

This walkthrough focuses on **Real-World Applications: Medallion at a High-Traffic E-Commerce Platform**.

Before making a design choice, clarify:

- An e-commerce marketplace processes 5 million orders per day, sourced from a mobile app, a web frontend, and a third-party reseller API.
- Each source emits events in a slightly different schema.
- The reseller API occasionally delivers duplicate events.

**Concepts in play:** data-warehousing-lakehouse, event-driven-architecture, database-indexing, jvm-internals-and-garbage-collection

## Stage 1 — Delta Lake: How ACID Guarantees Underpin the Medallion Pattern

- Delta Lake is the open-source table format that makes Medallion reliably implementable on object storage.
- Without Delta Lake (or a similar format like Apache Iceberg or Apache Hudi), running an UPDATE or DELETE on Parquet files in S3 is not atomic — a partial failure leaves the table in a corrupt state.
- Delta Lake solves this with a write-ahead transaction log ( delta log/ ) that records every operation as a JSON commit entry.
- Every read sees a consistent snapshot regardless of concurrent writes.

*Applies **data-warehousing-lakehouse** to the decision above.*

**Observable outcome:** Every read sees a consistent snapshot regardless of concurrent writes.

## End-to-end outcome

After working through the stages, you should be able to explain:

- Enforce Bronze immutability with IAM policies, not just convention.
- "We never mutate Bronze" is a convention that survives until the first incident where someone manually patches Bronze to fix a one-off problem.
- - Medallion Architecture is a design pattern, not a technology — it organizes a data lake into Bronze (raw), Silver (cleaned), and Gold (aggregated) zones with explicit contracts between them.
- - Bronze is sacred — it is the immutable source of truth that enables any downstream layer to be replayed from scratch when a bug is discovered.

## Alternatives considered

### Decision Guide: When to Use Medallion Architecture

At the end of this pipeline run, the CFO dashboard sees today's revenue broken down by product category, with duplicate orders removed, currency normalized, and all data validated against the Silver schema contract — from a single query against Gold, with zero cleaning code in the dashboard layer.


## Failure and degraded modes

The source does not isolate a separate failure mode. Limits that matter for the scenario are called out in the stage decisions above.
